newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index a shade lower at noon.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index a shade lower at noon.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index ended the morning session on Thursday slightly down in thin trading as investors waited for new market direction, analysts said.
The foreign currency B index lost 0.33 points or 0.22 percent to 151.01 on low turnover of HK$28.1 million.
"Investors are tired of goverment crackdown rumours," an analyst at PBI Securities said.
"The index will probably hover in a narrow band in the short term before China's strong economic fundamentals help boost it again," the analyst said.
The domestic currency A share index gained 3.98 points or 0.91 percent to 440.82 on turnover of 2.5 billion yuan.
Beijing began to implement policies to dampen stock speculation at the start of May, by which time the A and B indices had surged more than 50 percent from the beginning of 1997.
State media said on Thursday that China's central bank had set up two special phone lines for investors to report irregularities and illegal trading on the financial markets.
The move followed a similar announcement by the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) on Wednesday.
Shenzhen Benelux Enterprise Co Ltd was the worst performer in the B share market, losing HK$0.32 or 8.49 percent to HK$3.45.
